chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Majilawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from his father, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever says in his bowing, prostration, and standing:
O Allah, bestow prayer upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad,
Allah will record for him that [reward] equal to the reward of the bowing, prostration, and standing [in which it was recited].

key_terms.صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: Bestow blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Durood during the movements of Salat?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) highlights the immense virtue of integrating Durood into the physical postures of Salah, noting that the reward is multiplied to match the specific act performed. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on the spiritual efficacy of invoking blessings upon the Ahl al-Bayt as an integral component of worship, rather than merely a supplementary supplication. It reflects the broader theological principle that love and remembrance of the Prophet and his pure progeny are intrinsically linked to the acceptance and reward of individual acts of devotion.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: Allaahumma     s’alli     a’laa     muh’ammadinw     wa     aali muh’ammad
in his Ruku, his Sajdah and his Qiyam, Allah writes for him a reward like that of Ruku, Sajdah or Qiyam.”
